jobs.description:
At Solventum, we improve lives by helping healthcare professionals do their best work. Join a team using innovation and insight to make a real impact on the future of healthcare. All roles listed are with Solventum, and we’re committed to protecting your personal information—learn more in our Privacy Policy: https://www.solventum.com/en-us/home/legal/website-privacy-statement/applicant-privacy/

Job Description:

Job Description Summary:
Supporting IT execution during acquisition and divestiture transactions.

At Solventum, we enable better, smarter, safer healthcare to improve lives. As a new company with a long legacy of creating breakthrough solutions for our customers’ toughest challenges, we pioneer game-changing innovations at the intersection of health, material and data science that change patients' lives for the better while enabling healthcare professionals to perform at their best. Because people, and their wellbeing, are at the heart of every scientific advancement we pursue.
We partner closely with the brightest minds in healthcare to ensure that every solution we create melds the latest technology with compassion and empathy. Because at Solventum, we never stop solving for you.

The Impact You’ll Make in this Role

- Owning IT M&A execution strategy and delivery accountability across the transaction portfolio , setting the operating plan, execution frameworks, prioritization approach, and risk posture for concurrent acquisitions, divestitures, integrations, and separations, and delivering the outcomes committed to business and corporate development leadership.

- Shaping transaction outcomes from diligence through close and TSA exit by directing IT due diligence, transaction planning, TSA strategy, pricing inputs, service design, delivery, and exit sequencing, and by making judgment calls on transition approaches where precedent does not exist and the financial and operational stakes are material.

- Influencing enterprise strategic direction for M&A readiness by partnering with IT, business leadership, Corporate Development, IMO, HR, Legal, Finance, Procurement, Cybersecurity, Architecture, Infrastructure, Data, and Applications leaders to assess transaction feasibility, shape deal-shaping inputs, and align technology capability to inorganic growth and portfolio strategy.

- Serving as the GCC lead and senior advisor on IT M&A , counseling executive leadership on transaction risk, integration and separation strategy, operating model implications, resourcing trade-offs, cost and synergy exposure, and value realization, with decisions that regularly impact multiple IT and business areas as well as external counterparties.

- Owning and maturing the IT M&A capability as a global center of expertise , establishing the operating model, governance frameworks, methodologies, playbooks, tooling, talent model, and performance measures that determine how Solventum executes transactions at scale, and coaching practitioners across IT to build organizational readiness.

- Representing Solventum IT externally with acquirers, divestiture buyers, acquired and divested entities, advisors, and service providers , negotiating transition scope, service commitments, and exit terms, and resolving escalations that carry financial, contractual, and reputational consequence.

- Directing resource and investment planning for the transaction portfolio by assessing demand across deals, recommending funding and staffing allocations, managing third-party and partner capacity, and making prioritization recommendations that shape how IT resources are deployed against inorganic growth objectives.

Your Skills and Expertise

To set you up for success in this role from day one, Solventum requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:
- Master's degree or Diploma in Business Administration, Information Technology, Strategy, or a related discipline from a top-tier institute AND a minimum of 12 years of experience in Information Technology , including 8+ years supporting mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, integration, separation, or business transformation activities

OR
- Bachelor's Degree or higher from an accredited university, or High School Diploma/GED from an accredited institution, AND a minimum of 14 years of experience in Information Technology , including 8+ years supporting mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, integration, separation, or business transformation activities

AND In addition to the above requirements, the following are also required:

- Minimum 10+ years working with global IT organizations or IT consulting firms supporting complex technology programs, infrastructure, applications, cybersecurity, digital transformation, or enterprise technology initiatives as part of a Transformation or Deal Management Office.

- Demonstrated experience leading multiple concurrent, complex transactions end to end , with accountability for execution strategy, governance, delivery outcomes, and enterprise-level dependency, risk, and resource management.

- Demonstrated experience establishing or owning an M&A operating model, methodology, or center of expertise , including governance frameworks, playbooks, tooling, and capability development across a global organization.

- Demonstrated ability to advise and influence senior executives and external counterparties , including negotiating transition scope and service commitments, resolving high-stakes escalations, and driving decisions that impact multiple business areas and external parties

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:
- Experience leading IT due diligence, Day 1 readiness, TSA planning, TSA execution, TSA exit, integration, separation, or carve-out activities in a consulting firm or within an M&A or transformation office .

- Deep understanding of enterprise IT capabilities including infrastructure, applications, cybersecurity, architecture, digital workplace, data, and cloud technologies.

- Experience shaping deal-stage inputs such as technology diligence findings, cost and synergy estimates, TSA pricing, and separation feasibility assessments that inform transaction decisions.

- Demonstrated ability to resolve complex and ambiguous business challenges through structured analysis, executive engagement, and decisive recommendations.

- Proven ability to influence and negotiate at an expert level with audiences who may not be knowledgeable in the subject area, managing differing interests across IT, business, and external stakeholders.

- Experience coaching and developing practitioners across multiple projects or organizations, transferring M&A expertise and building bench strength.

- Familiarity with AI tools, Microsoft Power Platform, Smartsheet, Power BI , or similar collaboration and reporting technologies

Work location:
- Hybrid

Travel: May include up to 10%

Relocation Assistance: Is not authorized.

Supporting Your Well-being
Solventum offers many programs to help you live your best life – both physically and financially. To ensure competitive pay and benefits, Solventum regularly benchmarks with other companies that are comparable in size and scope.

Solventum is committed to maintaining the highest standards of integrity and professionalism in our recruitment process.  Applicants must remain alert to fraudulent job postings and recruitment schemes that falsely claim to represent Solventum and seek to exploit job seekers.

Job Description:

Job title: FMS FedRAMP Program Manager

At Solventum, we enable better, smarter, safer healthcare to improve lives. As a new company with a long legacy of creating breakthrough solutions for our customers’ toughest challenges, we pioneer game-changing innovations at the intersection of health, material and data science that change patients' lives for the better while enabling healthcare professionals to perform at their best. Because people, and their wellbeing, are at the heart of every scientific advancement we pursue.

We partner closely with the brightest minds in healthcare to ensure that every solution we create melds the latest technology with compassion and empathy. Because at Solventum, we never stop solving for you.

The Impact You’ll Make in this Role

The FedRAMP Program Manager is responsible for leading and managing the Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) security compliance program Key responsibilities include:
·         Partnering with Security, Business, and R&D and Business Development teams to ensure that RHSP continues to meet and maintain all authorization requirements for use by federal agencies.
·         Developing and managing FedRAMP project plans, schedules, and deliverables.
·         Support monitoring and management of associated contracts aligned to FedRAMP authorization to include 3PAO
·         Monitoring the status of System Security Plans (SSPs), Security and Privacy Policies and Procedures, POA&Ms, SARs, and other required documentation.  Partnering with the Security team as necessary to ensure all required updates are made accurately and on time.
·         Monitoring and managing vulnerabilities in the system, along with related remediation plans and tickets, tracking POA&M items, and ensuring timely resolution of all findings.
·         Leading and coordinating FedRAMP Continuous Monitoring efforts with the security team and other teams as needed (security, engineering, product, legal).  Submitting ConMon artifacts and deliverables to FedRAMP and federal agencies.
·         Preparing for and facilitating audits, assessments, and significant change in partnership with the security, business, and development teams.  Ensuring documentation updates, SCR forms, Security and Privacy Impact Assessments, and Change Control Board reviews are completed accurately and on time.
·         Interfacing with external audit teams to plan and coordinate audits, including evidence collection, document delivery, penetration testing, interviews, and any additional testing.
·         Acting as the central liaison between Solventum teams and federal agencies (including the FedRAMP PMO).  Facilitating conversations and resolving any issues to ensure continued authorization.
·         Educating internal stakeholders on FedRAMP requirements and ensuring continued compliance with FedRAMP and federal agency authorization requirements.
·         Maintaining up-to-date knowledge of FedRAMP and agency authorization requirements and processes.  Following all updates to FedRAMP, NIST 800-53, FISMA, CMMC, among others and government security frameworks.
·         Other assigned duties aligned to cybersecurity of our federal contracts and solutions

To set you up for success in this role from day one, Solventum requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:
- Bachelor’s Degree or higher AND 7 years of Program Management experience

OR
- High School Diploma/GED AND 11 years of Program Management experience
- Understanding FedRAMP, NIST 800-53, FISMA, CMMC and other government security frameworks
- Must be able to pass a government background check for a position of T5 Public Trust

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:

- Master’s degree in health informatics, cybersecurity, or the like from an accredited institution
- Experience briefing executive level personnel
- Experience within DoD and VA health care environments with direct responsibility for project or program management activities
- Ability to multi-task and handle large and sometimes complex workload under time constraints

Travel: 20%
Relocation Assistance: is not authorized
Location: Remote

Must be legally authorized to work in country of employment without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status).

Solventum offers many programs to help you live your best life – both physically and financially. To ensure competitive pay and benefits, Solventum regularly benchmarks with other companies that are comparable in size and scope.

See Solventum Announces Intent to Separate its Health Information Systems Business :: Solventum Corporation Newsroom . Any transaction would be subject to customary approvals, including approval by Solventum's Board of Directors, regulatory requirements and other customary conditions. This position supports the Health Information Systems Business. If a future transaction involving that business were to occur, the impact on this role would be determined as part of that process and would remain subject to applicable legal requirements, approvals and business decisions.
